answer: Because the island count is verified against the forge text itself, the fable audit records each rejection and the operator cannot amortise one paragraph. An answer claiming a deep mechanism must supply at least 6 distinct supporting claims, and the count is checked before grading so shallow text cannot pass by padding. Filling 115 aliases therefore means producing 115 separate sets of claims, which is authoring work rather than a lookup. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
